# Florence 1347 – Scientific method & philosophical ideas

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/europe-1347-florence.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Scientific method (conjecture, test, publish, repeat)** [`scientific_method`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_method.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Truth is sought by commentary and disputation on Aristotle. Workshops improve by trial, and Avicenna's rules for trying drugs are read. A repeatable test of a stated cause is unfamiliar. Local: dyers', goldsmiths' and assayers' workshops (trial and error); friars' schools at Santa Maria Novella and Santa Croce. Elsewhere: Paris, Jean Buridan and the arts faculty; Oxford, the Merton College calculators.
- **Test claims instead of trusting authority** [`empiricism_over_authority`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/empiricism_over_authority.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept low. Bodies are opened at Bologna to illustrate Galen and Avicenna, not to check them. Contradicting an authority from observation needs a striking demonstration and a respected sponsor. Local: physicians of the Arte dei Medici e Speziali; merchants, who trust their own ledgers over hearsay. Elsewhere: Bologna, anatomical teaching on the body since Mondino de' Liuzzi (d. 1326).
- **Controlled comparison (experiment with control group)** [`controlled_trial`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/controlled_trial.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Avicenna's Canon, the physicians' textbook, lists conditions for testing a drug. Nobody compares treated and untreated groups. Santa Maria Nuova has many patients with similar complaints. Local: Santa Maria Nuova hospital.
- **Placebo effect and blinded trials** [`placebo_blinding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/placebo_blinding.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. That faith, relics and imagination help healing is accepted. Deceiving a patient for the sake of a test would offend physicians and confessors.
- **Correlation, causation and confounding** [`correlation_causation_confounding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/correlation_causation_confounding.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Scholastic logic names the fallacy post hoc. Astrologers and physicians ignore it: Villani links floods, famine and bank failures to conjunctions and sins.
- **Selection and survivorship bias, fair sampling** [`selection_bias_sampling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/selection_bias_sampling.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Cicero's story of Diagoras and the votive tablets survives in manuscripts few have read. The miracle-working Madonna of Orsanmichele is hung with wax images from those who were cured. Local: Orsanmichele (wax ex-votos around the Madonna).
- **Measurement and quantification** [`measurement_quantification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/measurement_quantification.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Merchants, the mint and the commune count and weigh everything; Villani counts the city's mouths, schools, looms and revenues. Natural philosophy stays qualitative. Local: Giovanni Villani (statistics of Florence, c. 1338); Paolo dell'Abbaco's abacus school at Santa Trinita; assayers of the Zecca (mint); Pegolotti's merchant handbook. Elsewhere: Oxford, Merton calculators reckon with degrees of heat and speed.
- **Nature follows simple mathematical laws** [`mathematical_laws_of_nature`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mathematical_laws_of_nature.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Accepted for music, optics and the heavens. Earthly change is explained by qualities and purposes (Aristotle). Painters have no geometric perspective. Local: Paolo dell'Abbaco (abacus master and astronomer). Elsewhere: Oxford, Merton College: mean-speed theorem (c. 1335); Paris, Buridan's impetus.
- **Falsifiability (risky, testable predictions)** [`falsifiability`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/falsifiability.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. An astrologer's forecast or a physician's prognosis can be checked against events, and failures are explained away. Agreeing in advance what would refute a claim is new.
- **Fallibilism (all knowledge of nature is provisional)** [`fallibilism_provisional_knowledge`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fallibilism_provisional_knowledge.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Academic scepticism is known from Cicero and Augustine. Doubting Aristotle's certainties is risky: Nicholas of Autrecourt must burn his writings in Paris in November 1347. Elsewhere: Paris, Nicholas of Autrecourt (condemned at Avignon 1346).
- **Weighing evidence (base rates and Bayesian updating)** [`bayesian_reasoning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bayesian_reasoning.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Merchants revise their judgement when letters bring news of wars, wrecks or failures. No arithmetic of chance exists, so numbers for likelihood would be new.
- **Reproducibility and open publication** [`reproducibility_open_publication`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reproducibility_open_publication.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. No printing. A finding spreads by hand copies, letters, sermons and council decrees. Guilds guard recipes and fine members who reveal them. Local: cartolai (stationers) and copyists; notaries, who can certify a witnessed result.
- **Systematic errors of human judgement (cognitive biases)** [`cognitive_biases`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cognitive_biases.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium
- **Formal logic (valid deduction and fallacies)** [`formal_logic`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/formal_logic.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Aristotelian syllogistic and the fallacies are school subjects (Peter of Spain). Ockham dies at Munich in April 1347. No symbolic logic. Local: Dominican school at Santa Maria Novella; Franciscan school at Santa Croce; Augustinians of Santo Spirito. Elsewhere: Paris, Jean Buridan; Bologna and Padua, arts faculties.
- **Parsimony (Occam's razor)** [`occams_razor`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/occams_razor.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Scholastics know the maxim against needless entities. Its best-known user, Ockham, died excommunicate in 1347, and Paris restricted Ockhamist teaching in 1339–40. Elsewhere: Paris and Oxford, nominalist masters.
- **Thought experiment** [`thought_experiment`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/thought_experiment.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Scholastics argue from imagined cases (secundum imaginationem). The conclusions count as exercises in logic, not as findings about nature. Elsewhere: Paris, Jean Buridan.
- **Source criticism (testing documents and reports)** [`source_criticism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/source_criticism.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Notaries and canon lawyers test charters by seals, hands and formulas. Chroniclers repeat the legends of Troy and Fiesole. Petrarch hunts and compares old manuscripts. Local: Arte dei Giudici e Notai; Giovanni Villani (legend and counted fact side by side). Elsewhere: Avignon and Vaucluse, Petrarch (found Cicero's letters at Verona, 1345).
- **Consent and ethics of experiments on people** [`informed_consent_research_ethics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/informed_consent_research_ethics.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Physicians know the Hippocratic duty to do no harm. Hospitals and courts hold power over the poor and prisoners; asking a subject's consent to a trial is unheard of.
- **Natural causes (naturalism about disease, weather, comets)** [`natural_causes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/natural_causes.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Aristotle's Meteorology gives natural causes for comets, quakes and floods; all are also read as signs. After the 1333 flood Florentines debated nature against divine judgement. Local: Giovanni Villani (records the 1333 debate and the comet of 1347). Elsewhere: Paris, medical faculty: plague from the conjunction of 1345 (opinion of October 1348).
- **Scepticism towards astrology, omens, witchcraft and transmutation** [`scepticism_superstition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scepticism_superstition.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Astrology is respected learning; only its denial of free will is heresy (Cecco d'Ascoli, burned in Florence 1327). Dante puts diviners and alchemists in Hell as frauds. Local: Paolo dell'Abbaco (astrologer); Franciscan inquisitor at Santa Croce. Elsewhere: Avignon, John XXII's decretal against alchemists (1317).
- **Atomism (matter is made of tiny particles in motion)** [`atomism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atomism.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Known only through Aristotle's refutation; Lucretius is lost. Dante has Democritus set the world upon chance and buries Florentine Epicureans among the heretics. Elsewhere: Paris, Nicholas of Autrecourt argued atoms as probable as Aristotle's forms; condemned 1346.
- **The same physical laws on earth and in the heavens** [`universal_physical_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_physical_laws.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. The heavens are a fifth, changeless element moved by intelligences; below the Moon the four elements. Buridan suggests one impetus could keep the spheres turning. Elsewhere: Paris, Jean Buridan.
- **Mechanical philosophy (explain by matter and motion, not hidden purposes)** [`mechanical_philosophy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mechanical_philosophy.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Millwrights and the builders of the new weight-driven clocks think in wheels and weights. Philosophers explain by forms and purposes; matter and motion alone sounds Epicurean.
- **Idea of progress (knowledge accumulates, the future can be better)** [`idea_of_progress`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/idea_of_progress.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Florentines are proud of new things: spectacles, the florin, the campanile. Fra Giordano preached in 1306 that new arts are found every day. Scholars still look backwards. Local: memory of Fra Giordano da Pisa's sermons at Santa Maria Novella.
- **Invention as a method (organised research and development)** [`systematic_invention`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/systematic_invention.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Masters improve by trial inside one workshop and keep results secret. The cathedral works decide by models and committees of masters. Nobody funds invention as such. Local: Opera del Duomo (cathedral and campanile works); Zecca (mint). Elsewhere: Venice, the Arsenal; Paris, Guido da Vigevano's book of war machines (1335).
- **Golden rule and universal ethics** [`golden_rule_universal_ethics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/golden_rule_universal_ethics.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Matthew 7:12 is preached from every pulpit. It is not applied to enemies of the commune, heretics, Jews or the magnates under the Ordinances of Justice.
- **Human equality and dignity** [`human_equality_dignity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/human_equality_dignity.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Souls are equal before God; ranks on earth are natural. The popolo distrusts noble birth, yet wool workers and peasants have no voice.
- **Natural (human) rights** [`natural_rights`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/natural_rights.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Canon lawyers and Franciscans argue about natural law and rights in the poverty dispute. In practice entitlements follow citizenship, guild membership and status. Local: Franciscans of Santa Croce; Fraticelli sympathisers in Tuscany. Elsewhere: Perugia, Bartolus of Sassoferrato.
- **Social contract (government by consent)** [`social_contract`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/social_contract.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The popolo holds that the city governs itself and that it lawfully drove out the Duke of Athens (1343). Marsilius of Padua's version is condemned as heresy. Local: priors and guild consuls; St Anne's day (26 July), feast of the expulsion. Elsewhere: Perugia, Bartolus: a free city is its own prince.
- **Freedom of thought, speech and the press** [`freedom_of_speech_thought`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/freedom_of_speech_thought.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Councils debate, but speaking against the regime or the faith is punished. Cecco d'Ascoli was burned here in 1327. In 1346 the commune curbed the inquisitor's powers. Local: Franciscan inquisitor at Santa Croce; Palazzo del Podestà.
- **Religious toleration and freedom of conscience** [`religious_tolerance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/religious_tolerance.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept low. Heresy is a crime. Few Jews live in Florence itself. In 1348–49 Jews north of the Alps are murdered as well-poisoners; talk of invisible poison in water feeds that. Local: Jewish lenders in smaller Tuscan towns. Elsewhere: Avignon, Clement VI (bulls protecting Jews, 1348); Mongol khanates, clergy of all faiths exempted.
- **Secular state (separation of religious and civil authority)** [`secular_state`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/secular_state.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. Dante's Monarchia and Marsilius argue it; both are condemned. Guelf Florence banks for the pope, yet in 1346 it limited clerical privileges and was put under interdict. Elsewhere: Munich, court of Ludwig of Bavaria (dies October 1347).
- **Utilitarianism (judge rules by their consequences for everyone)** [`utilitarianism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/utilitarianism.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. The common good (bene comune) is standard civic and Dominican rhetoric. It means the city's peace and honour, not a sum of everyone's welfare. Local: memory of Remigio de' Girolami's De bono communi (Santa Maria Novella). Elsewhere: Siena, Lorenzetti's frescoes of good and bad government (1338–39).
- **Abolition of judicial torture; proportionate, certain punishment** [`abolition_of_torture`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abolition_of_torture.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Torture by the rope is ordinary procedure under Roman law, and confession is the best proof. The foreign judges of podestà and captain apply it. Local: Palazzo del Podestà; Stinche prison.
- **Positive-sum cooperation (trade is not zero-sum)** [`positive_sum_cooperation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/positive_sum_cooperation.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Merchants live by mutual gain and scholastics defend honest trade. Policy between cities and guilds is zero-sum: bans, reprisals, tolls and wars for Lucca. Local: Arte di Calimala; Mercanzia.
- **Game theory (prisoner's dilemma, credible commitment)** [`game_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/game_theory.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Merchants, ambassadors and mercenary captains reason this way by instinct. There are no words for it.
- **Commons problem and how communities solve it** [`tragedy_of_the_commons`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tragedy_of_the_commons.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Rural communes regulate woods, pasture and water by statute. Monastic forests are managed for the long term. Mills and fish weirs crowd the Arno. Local: Camaldoli and Vallombrosa forests; village statutes of the contado.
